hints.content:
The basic function $\sin(x)$ intersects its midline at $(0,0)$ and has a maximum point at $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},1\right)$.

$\qquad$![](${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/a341a449700483900a5e0b9fc1fc0ab4.png)

Let's transform $\pink{\sin(x)}$ to $\blue{2\sin\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)+4}$ step by step and see how the graph changes along the way.

The transformation from $\pink{\sin(x)}$ to $\green{\sin\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x\right)}$ is a horizontal stretch by a factor of $\dfrac{1}{\frac{1}{3}}=3$, so the maximum point's horizontal distance from the origin is stretched from $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ to $\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

The transformation from $\green{\sin\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x\right)}$ to $\red{2\sin\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x\right)}$ is a vertical stretch by a factor of $2$, so the maximum point's vertical distance from the origin is stretched from $1$ to $2$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 2]]

options.alt: A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (pi over two, one). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (three pi over two, one).

A dashed graph and a solid graph trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi and the y axis scales by one. On the dashed graph there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (three pi over two, one). On the solid graph, there is a point on the graph at the midline at (zero, zero) and a point at the maximum next to the mentioned point at (three pi over two, two).

hints.content: The transformation from $\red{2\sin\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x\right)}$ to $\blue{2\sin\left(\dfrac{1}{3}x-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)+4}$, which is equivalent to $2\sin\left(\dfrac{1}{3}(x-\pi)\right)+4$, is a translation to the right by $\pi$ units and a translation upwards by $4$ units.

As a result of these transformations, the intersection point with the midline is now at $\left(\pi,4\right)$ and the maximum point is at $(2.5\pi,6)$.

The resulting graph looks as follows:

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A graph of a trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x axis scales by pi and the y axis scales by one. There is a point on the graph at the midline at (pi, four) and a point on the maximum next to the mentioned point at (two and one half pi, six).

*Note that one moveable point always defines an extremum point in the graph and the other point always defines a neighbouring intersection with the midline.*
